description: Governed calibration for the deterministic CVSS-Environmental VDR PAIN classifier. These are the ONLY tunable knobs in the method: the word thresholds, the EPSS likely-exploitable threshold, the impact/requirement weights, and the tag-to-requirement maps. The FedRAMP VDR-TFR-PVR remediation-day matrix is NOT here: it is FedRAMP's, read at build time from the pinned machine-readable rules in infrastructure/schemas/fedramp-rules/ (never typed into code). Only the classifier is ours to tune; the deadlines are not.
method_reference: A Deterministic, CVSS-Environmental Method for FedRAMP Rev5 VDR/VER Vulnerability Prioritization (informational memo, June 2026); CVSS v3.1 Environmental metric group (Modified Impact Sub-Score, CR/IR/AR).
epss_threshold_rationale: FIRST publishes no universal EPSS threshold; the right one depends on remediation capacity, risk tolerance and asset context. 0.10 is the value FIRST notes is commonly cited. At 0.10 a finding is likely exploitable once its estimated chance of exploitation activity in the next 30 days reaches 10%, a remediation volume this system can sustain. Known-exploited and actively exploited findings are LEV regardless of score. Revisited when remediation capacity changes or as EPSS's record on this system builds up.
likely_overdue_margin_rationale: REQ-DLN-2: an open finding is reported likely overdue once five days or fewer remain before its deadline. Five days matches the Class C evaluation window (VER-TFR-EVU): one operator needs at least that long to schedule, ship and verify a fix, so with less time left the deadline is likely to be missed.
